flows.name: Visit the landing page
flows.goal: Understand what SoloStudio is for and get started.

steps.userAction: The visitor opens the landing page.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows that SoloStudio is a single workspace for a solo freelance designer to manage clients, projects and bookings, with options to sign up, sign in, and a link to the public booking page.

steps.userAction: The visitor chooses to sign up, sign in, or open the public booking page.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the chosen starting point: the sign-up form, the sign-in form, or the public booking page.

flows.outcome: Nothing changes; the visitor knows how to sign up, sign in or open the booking page.

flows.name: Sign up
flows.goal: Create an account to get a private workspace.

steps.userAction: The visitor chooses to sign up.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the sign-up form.

steps.userAction: The visitor fills in the form and submits it.
steps.websiteResponse: The website creates the account and private workspace with the three pre-created session types and empty weekly availability, signs the designer in and shows the home dashboard.

alternatives.condition: The email is not an address or the password is shorter than 8 characters.

steps.websiteResponse: The website marks the field that is wrong and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the typed values and offers to try again.

alternatives.condition: The email already has an account.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says the email already has an account and offers to sign in instead.

steps.userAction: The visitor chooses to sign in.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the sign-in form.

flows.outcome: The designer has an account and private workspace and is signed in; after refresh still signed in.

flows.name: Sign in
flows.goal: Sign in to the private workspace.

steps.userAction: The visitor chooses to sign in.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the sign-in form.

steps.userAction: The visitor fills in the form and submits it.
steps.websiteResponse: The website checks the account, signs the designer in and shows the home dashboard with today's sessions, follow-ups due this week and overdue tasks.

alternatives.condition: The email is not an address or the password is shorter than 8 characters.

steps.websiteResponse: The website marks the field that is wrong and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the typed values and offers to try again.

alternatives.condition: The email and password match no account.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says no account matches and offers to try again or sign up instead.

steps.userAction: The visitor chooses to sign up.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the sign-up form.

flows.outcome: The designer is signed in and sees the home dashboard; after refresh still signed in.

flows.name: Sign out
flows.goal: Leave the workspace signed out.

steps.userAction: The designer chooses to sign out.
steps.websiteResponse: The website signs her out and shows the public landing page.

flows.outcome: The designer is signed out; after refresh she stays signed out.

flows.name: See the home dashboard
flows.goal: See what needs attention today in one place.

steps.userAction: The designer opens the home dashboard.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows today's sessions with their bookings, follow-ups due this week with overdue first, and overdue tasks, each linking to the relevant client, session or project.

alternatives.condition: There are no sessions today, no follow-ups due this week and no overdue tasks.

steps.websiteResponse: The website shows that everything is clear and offers to go to clients, projects, sessions, availability and session types.

flows.outcome: Nothing changes; the designer has seen today's sessions, follow-ups due this week and overdue tasks.

flows.name: Browse clients
flows.goal: Find clients and see who needs a follow-up first.

steps.userAction: The designer opens the client list.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows all clients sorted with overdue follow-ups first then soonest due, each showing name, company, status and follow-up due state.

steps.userAction: The designer searches by name or company and filters by status.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows only the matching clients in the same follow-up order.

steps.userAction: The designer opens a client from the list.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows that client's details, notes, projects and bookings.
The website says there are no clients yet and offers to add a client.

alternatives.condition: No clients match the search or filter.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says nothing matches and offers to clear the search or filter.

alternatives.condition: The client was deleted in the meantime.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says the client is gone and shows the client list.

flows.outcome: Nothing changes; the designer has seen the sorted client list.

flows.name: View a client
flows.goal: See one client's details, notes, projects and bookings in one place.

steps.userAction: The designer opens a client from the client list.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the client's name, email, company, profile and status together with its dated notes with follow-up dates, its projects and its bookings matched by email.

alternatives.condition: The client has no notes, projects or bookings yet.

steps.websiteResponse: The website shows empty notes, projects and bookings sections with offers to add a note or a project.

alternatives.condition: The client was deleted in the meantime.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says the client is gone and shows the client list.

flows.outcome: Nothing changes; the designer has seen the client's details, notes, projects and bookings.

flows.name: Add a client
flows.goal: Remember a new client.

steps.userAction: The designer chooses to add a client.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty client form with status already set to Lead.

steps.userAction: The designer fills in the client and saves it.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the client and shows it in the client list and as a client page.

alternatives.condition: The name is empty, the email is not an address, or the status is missing.

steps.websiteResponse: The website marks what is wrong and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the values and offers to try again.
Nothing is saved; the website shows the client list as it was.

flows.outcome: A new client is saved and still there after refresh.

flows.name: Edit a client
flows.goal: Change a client's details or status.

steps.userAction: The designer chooses to edit the client.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the client form filled with the current name, email, company, profile and status.

steps.userAction: The designer changes values and saves them.
steps.websiteResponse: The website updates the client and shows the updated client details.

alternatives.condition: The client was deleted in the meantime.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says the client is gone and shows the client list.

alternatives.condition: The name is empty, the email is not an address, or the status is missing.

steps.websiteResponse: The website marks what is wrong and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the values and offers to try again.
Nothing is changed; the website shows the client again as it was.

flows.outcome: The client is updated and stays updated after refresh.

flows.name: Delete a client
flows.goal: Remove a client and everything under them.

steps.userAction: The designer chooses Delete on the client.
steps.websiteResponse: The website asks the designer to confirm deleting the client with its notes, projects and tasks, explaining its bookings will stay visible without a client link.
The website shows the client list without the client.
Nothing is deleted; the website shows the client again, unchanged.

alternatives.condition: The client was deleted in the meantime.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says the client is already gone and shows the client list.

flows.outcome: The client, its notes, projects and tasks are gone after refresh; its bookings remain unlinked.

flows.name: Add a note with a follow-up date
flows.goal: Jot a dated note after a call and optionally set a follow-up.

steps.userAction: The designer chooses to add a note.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty note form with the note date set to today.

steps.userAction: The designer fills in the note and saves it.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the note under the client and shows it with its follow-up date in the client's notes.

alternatives.condition: The note text is empty or a date cannot be understood.

steps.websiteResponse: The website marks the field that needs fixing and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the entered values and offers to try again.

alternatives.condition: The designer cancels adding the note.

steps.websiteResponse: Nothing is saved; the website shows the client as it was.

flows.outcome: The new dated note with its follow-up date is saved under the client after refresh.

flows.name: Edit a note
flows.goal: Correct or update a note and its follow-up date.

steps.userAction: The designer chooses to edit a note under the client.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the note form filled with the note's current text, note date and follow-up date.

steps.userAction: The designer changes the values and saves the note.
steps.websiteResponse: The website updates the note and shows it under the client with its new follow-up date.

alternatives.condition: The note text is empty or a date cannot be understood.

steps.websiteResponse: The website marks the field that needs fixing and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the entered values and offers to try again.

alternatives.condition: The designer cancels editing the note.

steps.websiteResponse: Nothing is changed; the website shows the note as it was.

alternatives.condition: The note is no longer there.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says the note is gone and shows the client's remaining notes.

flows.outcome: The note is updated and stays updated after refresh.

flows.name: Delete a note
flows.goal: Remove a note that is no longer needed.

steps.userAction: The designer chooses Delete on a note under the client.
steps.websiteResponse: The website asks the designer to confirm deleting the note.
The website shows the client's remaining notes without the deleted note.
The website shows the note again, unchanged.
The website says the note is gone and shows the client's remaining notes.

flows.outcome: The note is gone and stays gone after refresh.

flows.name: Mark a follow-up done
flows.goal: Mark a follow-up done with one click.
preconditions: At least one note with a follow-up date exists.

steps.userAction: The designer marks a follow-up done with one click.
steps.websiteResponse: The website clears the follow-up date and shows the client no longer due for a follow-up.
The website keeps the follow-up date and offers to try again.

alternatives.condition: The note is no longer there.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says the note is gone and shows the client list as it is.

flows.outcome: The follow-up date is cleared and stays cleared after refresh.

flows.name: Push a follow-up a week
flows.goal: Push a follow-up a week with one click.
preconditions: At least one note with a follow-up date exists.

steps.userAction: The designer pushes a follow-up a week with one click.
steps.websiteResponse: The website adds 7 days to the follow-up date and shows the new due date in sorted order.
The website keeps the follow-up date and offers to try again.

alternatives.condition: The note is no longer there.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says the note is gone and shows the client list as it is.

flows.outcome: The follow-up date is 7 days later and stays so after refresh.

flows.name: Browse projects
flows.goal: See every project and how much work is left.

steps.userAction: The designer opens the projects view.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows all projects with their name, client name, due date and open task count and that each row links to its project and client.

steps.userAction: The designer searches by project name or client name.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows only projects whose name or client name matches.
The website shows that there are no projects yet and offers to add a project.
The website shows that nothing matches and offers to clear the search or add a project.

flows.outcome: Nothing changes; the designer has seen all projects with open task counts.

flows.name: View a project with its tasks
flows.goal: See a project's tasks and narrow them down.

steps.userAction: The designer opens a project from the projects view.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the project's name, description, due date and client together with its tasks grouped by status, with overdue tasks standing out.

steps.userAction: The designer searches by title and filters by status and priority.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows only tasks whose title matches and whose status and priority match the chosen filters.

alternatives.condition: The project was deleted in the meantime.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says the project is gone and shows the projects view.

alternatives.condition: The project has no tasks yet.

steps.websiteResponse: The website shows that there are no tasks yet and offers to add a task.

alternatives.condition: No task matches the search or filters.

steps.websiteResponse: The website shows that nothing matches and offers to clear the search and filters.

flows.outcome: Nothing changes; the designer has seen the project and its filtered tasks.

flows.name: Add a project
flows.goal: Start a new project for a client.

steps.userAction: The designer chooses to add a project.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty project form.

steps.userAction: The designer fills in the project and saves it.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the project under the chosen client and shows it in the projects view.

alternatives.condition: The name or description is empty, the due date is not a date, or no client is chosen.

steps.websiteResponse: The website marks what is missing or wrong and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the values and offers to try again.
Nothing is saved; the website shows the projects view as it was.

flows.outcome: The new project is saved and still there after refresh.

flows.name: Edit a project
flows.goal: Change a project's details or move it to another client.

steps.userAction: The designer chooses to edit the project.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the project form with the current name, description, due date and client.

steps.userAction: The designer changes the project and saves it.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the changes and shows the updated project.

alternatives.condition: The project was deleted in the meantime.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says the project is gone and shows the projects view.

alternatives.condition: The name or description is empty, the due date is not a date, or no client is chosen.

steps.websiteResponse: The website marks what is missing or wrong and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the values and offers to try again.
Nothing is changed; the website shows the project as it was.

flows.outcome: The project is updated and stays updated after refresh.

flows.name: Delete a project
flows.goal: Remove a project and its tasks.

steps.userAction: The designer chooses to delete the project.
steps.websiteResponse: The website asks the designer to confirm deleting the project and its tasks.
The website deletes the project and its tasks and shows the projects view without the project.
Nothing is deleted; the website shows the project as it was.
The website says the project is already gone and shows the projects view.

flows.outcome: The project and its tasks are gone after refresh.

flows.name: Add a task
flows.goal: Add a task to a project.

steps.userAction: The designer chooses to add a task.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty task form with status set to To do and priority set to Medium.

steps.userAction: The designer fills in the task and saves it.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the task and shows it in the project's task list, standing out when its due date is before today and it is not Done.
The website marks the empty title and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the entered values and offers to try again.

alternatives.condition: The designer cancels adding the task.

steps.websiteResponse: Nothing is saved; the website shows the project with its tasks as they were.

flows.outcome: The new task is saved under the project after refresh.

flows.name: Edit a task
flows.goal: Change a task's title, status, priority or due date.

steps.userAction: The designer opens a task from the project's task list.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the task form with the task's current title, status, priority and due date.

steps.userAction: The designer changes the values and saves them.
steps.websiteResponse: The website updates the task and shows the updated task list with updated open counts.

alternatives.condition: The task was deleted in the meantime.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says the task is gone and shows the project's remaining tasks.
The website marks the empty title and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the entered values and offers to try again.
Nothing is changed; the website shows the project with its tasks as they were.

flows.outcome: The task is updated and stays updated after refresh.

flows.name: Delete a task
flows.goal: Remove a task that is no longer needed.

steps.userAction: The designer chooses Delete on a task.
steps.websiteResponse: The website asks the designer to confirm deleting the task.
The website shows the project's remaining tasks with updated open counts.
Nothing is deleted; the website shows the project with its tasks as they were.
The website says the task is gone and shows the project's remaining tasks.

flows.outcome: The task is gone and stays gone after refresh.

flows.name: Tick a task done
flows.goal: Tick a task done quickly.
preconditions: At least one open task exists.

steps.userAction: The designer ticks an open task done.
steps.websiteResponse: The website marks the task Done, updates the open task counts and no longer shows it as overdue.
The website keeps the task as it was and offers to try again.

alternatives.condition: The task was deleted in the meantime.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says the task is gone and shows the project's remaining tasks.
The website shows the task as Done with updated open counts.

flows.outcome: The task is Done and stays Done after refresh.

flows.name: Set weekly availability
flows.goal: Set the weekly days and hours that can be booked.

steps.userAction: The designer changes the days, from time and to time and saves them.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the weekly availability and shows the saved days and hours; future open slots use the new hours and existing bookings are unchanged.

alternatives.condition: At least one day is selected but From time or To time is missing, or To time is not after From time.

steps.websiteResponse: The website marks what is missing or wrong, keeps the entered days and times, and offers to correct them.
The website keeps the entered days and times and offers to try again.

flows.outcome: Availability is updated and still shows after refresh; existing bookings are unchanged.

flows.name: Browse session types
flows.goal: See the kinds of sessions visitors can book.

steps.userAction: The designer opens session types.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows all session types with their name, duration in minutes, displayed price and maximum people.

alternatives.condition: There are no session types yet.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says there are no session types yet and offers to add one.

flows.outcome: Nothing changes; the designer has seen all session types.

flows.name: Add a session type
flows.goal: Offer a new kind of bookable session.

steps.userAction: The designer chooses to add a session type.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty session type form.

steps.userAction: The designer fills in the session type and saves it.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the session type and shows it in the session type list.

alternatives.condition: The name is empty, the duration is not a whole number or is below 15 or above 480, the displayed price is not a number or is negative, or the maximum people is not a whole number or is below 1 or above 20.

steps.websiteResponse: The website marks what is wrong and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the values and offers to try again.
Nothing is saved; the website shows the session type list as it was.

flows.outcome: The new session type is saved and still there after refresh.

flows.name: Edit a session type
flows.goal: Change a session's length, displayed price or seats.
preconditions: At least one session type exists.

steps.userAction: The designer opens a session type to edit it.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the session type with its current name, duration in minutes, displayed price and maximum people in the session type form.

steps.userAction: The designer changes the values and saves them.
steps.websiteResponse: The website updates the session type and shows it in the session type list; existing bookings are unchanged.
The website says the session type is gone and shows the session type list.

alternatives.condition: The name is empty, the duration is not a whole number or is below 15 or above 480, the displayed price is not a number or is negative, or the maximum people is not a whole number or is below 1 or above 20.

steps.websiteResponse: The website marks what is wrong and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the values and offers to try again.
Nothing is changed; the website shows the session type list as it was.

flows.outcome: The session type is updated and stays updated after refresh; existing bookings are unchanged.

flows.name: See upcoming sessions
flows.goal: See upcoming sessions and who booked them.

steps.userAction: The designer opens upcoming sessions.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows upcoming slots with their session type, time and bookings, including full slots, and past sessions separately.
The website says there are no upcoming sessions yet and explains new sessions appear when guests book open times, and the designer can check availability and session types.

flows.outcome: Nothing changes; the designer has seen upcoming slots with their bookings.

flows.name: View a slot
flows.goal: See who booked a time slot and for what.
preconditions: At least one slot with or without bookings exists.

steps.userAction: The designer opens a slot from upcoming sessions.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the slot's time and session type with its bookings showing name, email and linked client.

alternatives.condition: The slot has no bookings yet.

steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the slot with no bookings yet and says the time stays open for booking until the slot is cancelled.
The website says the slot is gone and shows upcoming sessions.

flows.outcome: Nothing changes; the designer has seen the slot and its bookings.

flows.name: Cancel a slot
flows.goal: Cancel a time slot and everyone booked on it.
preconditions: At least one upcoming slot exists.

steps.userAction: The designer chooses to cancel the slot.
steps.websiteResponse: The website asks the designer to confirm cancelling the slot and every booking on it.
The website cancels the slot and every booking on it and shows upcoming sessions without the slot.
Nothing is cancelled; the website shows the slot again unchanged.
The website says the slot is gone and shows upcoming sessions.

flows.outcome: The slot and its bookings are cancelled and stay cancelled after refresh.

flows.name: View a booking as designer
flows.goal: See who booked, for what and when.

steps.userAction: The designer opens a booking from the upcoming sessions.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the booking's name, email, session type, slot time and linked client when one exists, with ways to open the client and the slot.

alternatives.condition: The booking was cancelled in the meantime.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says the booking is gone and shows the upcoming sessions.

flows.outcome: Nothing changes; the designer has seen the booking details.

flows.name: Open the public booking page
flows.goal: Arrive at the public booking page and get started.

steps.userAction: The visitor opens the public booking page using the designer's booking link.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows what booking is for, the session types with duration and displayed price, and how to start by picking a session type.

steps.userAction: The visitor chooses to continue to open times.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the session type choice to continue toward finding an open time.

alternatives.condition: No session types are offered right now.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says no sessions are currently offered and to check back later.

flows.outcome: Nothing changes; the guest knows how to pick a session type and see open times.

flows.name: Find an open slot
flows.goal: Pick a service and see which times are still open.

steps.userAction: The guest picks a session type.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the session type's duration and displayed price and lists its open slots for the next two weeks, excluding full slots and times blocked by overlapping bookings.

steps.userAction: The guest picks an open slot to book.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the chosen session type and slot with the booking details form.

alternatives.condition: There are no open slots for the chosen session type in the next two weeks.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says there are no open times for the chosen session type in the next two weeks and offers to try another session type.

alternatives.condition: The chosen slot became full or blocked by an overlapping booking before the guest picked it.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says that time is no longer open and shows the updated list of open slots for the chosen session type.

flows.outcome: Nothing changes; the guest has seen open slots for the chosen session type.

flows.name: Book a session
flows.goal: Book an open time and get a confirmation with a cancellation link.

steps.userAction: The guest chooses a session type.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows open slots for the next two weeks for that session type with its duration and displayed price, hiding full slots and times blocked by another booking.

steps.userAction: The guest chooses an open slot.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the chosen session type and slot time with the booking details form.

steps.userAction: The guest fills in name and email and confirms the booking.
steps.websiteResponse: The website creates the booking, links it to the client with the same email or creates a new Lead client when the email is new, and shows a confirmation with the booking time and the private cancellation link.

alternatives.condition: There are no open slots for the chosen session type in the next two weeks.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says no times are open for that session type and invites the guest to choose another session type.

alternatives.condition: The name is empty or the email is not an address.

steps.websiteResponse: The website marks what is wrong and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the entered values and offers to try again.

alternatives.condition: The slot became full or was cancelled before the booking was saved.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says the time is no longer open and invites the guest to choose another open slot.

flows.outcome: The booking is saved and the confirmation with cancellation link is shown; refresh still shows the booking as booked.

flows.name: Open a booking via its link
flows.goal: Check a booking's time and status.

steps.userAction: The guest opens the private cancellation link.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the booking's session type, slot time and status with the name and email it was booked with, and the option to cancel it.

alternatives.condition: The link is unknown or the booking no longer exists.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says the link is not recognised and offers to open the public booking page.

steps.userAction: The guest chooses to open the public booking page.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the public booking page with session types.
The website shows the booking as cancelled with its former time and offers to book another time.

flows.outcome: Nothing changes; the guest has seen the booking details.

flows.name: Cancel own booking
flows.goal: Cancel a booking and free the seat.
preconditions: Has the cancellation link for an active booking.

steps.userAction: The guest opens the private cancellation link.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the booking's session type, slot time and status with the option to cancel it.

steps.userAction: The guest chooses to cancel the booking.
steps.websiteResponse: The website asks the guest to confirm cancelling only this booking.

alternatives.condition: The link is unknown or the booking no longer exists.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says the link is not recognised and offers to open the public booking page.

steps.userAction: The guest chooses to open the public booking page.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the public booking page with session types.
The website shows the booking as already cancelled with its former time and offers to book another time.
The website cancels only that person's booking, frees the seat and shows the booking as cancelled.
Nothing is cancelled; the website shows the booking again unchanged.
The website keeps the booking unchanged and offers to try again.

flows.outcome: The booking is cancelled and stays cancelled after refresh; the seat is open again.

flows.name: Manage account
flows.goal: See and change the sign-in email and password.

steps.userAction: The designer opens account settings.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the current sign-in email with options to change the email and password.

steps.userAction: The designer changes the email and password and saves.
steps.websiteResponse: The website updates the account and shows the updated sign-in email.

alternatives.condition: The email is not an address or the password is shorter than 8 characters.

steps.websiteResponse: The website marks the field that is wrong and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the typed values and offers to try again.

alternatives.condition: The new email already has another account.

steps.websiteResponse: The website says the email is already in use and keeps the current sign-in email unchanged.

flows.outcome: The email and password are updated and stay updated after refresh; the designer stays signed in.

fields.label: Email
fields.meaning: How the designer signs in

fields.label: Password
fields.meaning: Secret that protects the designer's workspace

fields.label: Name
fields.meaning: How the designer refers to the client

fields.label: Email
fields.meaning: How to reach the client and match bookings to the client

fields.label: Company
fields.meaning: Client company when the client is a business

fields.label: Profile
fields.meaning: What the client does, how they met and what they pay
fields.example: Runs a D2C skincare brand, met at a meetup, pays 80000 per project

fields.label: Status
fields.meaning: Where the client is in the relationship

fields.label: Note text
fields.meaning: What was discussed or observed after a call
fields.example: Call about homepage redo, likes calm layouts, send proposal

fields.label: Note date
fields.meaning: The day the note is about, defaults to today

fields.label: Follow-up date
fields.meaning: When to follow up next, empty when no follow-up is needed

fields.label: Name
fields.meaning: How the designer refers to the project

fields.label: Description
fields.meaning: What the project covers in a few words

fields.label: Due date
fields.meaning: When the project should be finished, empty when none

fields.label: Client
fields.meaning: Which client the project belongs to

fields.label: Title
fields.meaning: What needs to be done

fields.label: Status
fields.meaning: Where the task is in the work

fields.label: Priority
fields.meaning: How urgent the task is

fields.label: Due date
fields.meaning: When the task should be done, empty when none

fields.label: Days
fields.meaning: Which weekdays the designer can be booked

fields.label: From time
fields.meaning: When bookable hours start on the chosen days

fields.label: To time
fields.meaning: When bookable hours end on the chosen days

fields.label: Name
fields.meaning: How visitors recognise the kind of session

fields.label: Duration in minutes
fields.meaning: How long one slot of this type lasts

fields.label: Displayed price
fields.meaning: Price shown for information only, nobody pays in the app

fields.label: Maximum people

assumptions.text: Client list offers search by name or company and filter by status; project task list offers search by title and filters by status and priority. Client sorting follows A02 (overdue follow-ups first, then soonest due). Task overdue highlighting follows A03.

New Tasks default to status To do and priority Medium unless the designer changes them. SessionTypes cannot be deleted in MVP to protect existing Slots and Bookings; the designer edits or adds types instead. There is no profile or preferences screen beyond sign-up and sign-in for the single designer.
Weekly Availability is pre-created at sign-up as empty with no days selected and is managed only by editing in F25; until hours are set no Slots are offered.

questions.question: Should past sessions and cancelled bookings remain visible to the designer?
questions.whyItMatters: This changes whether Slot and Booking history is kept or disappears after the time passes.
questions.defaultAnswer: Past slots and bookings stay visible in a past list and cannot be booked or cancelled.
